issues: Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 1: items 13 and 14 are combined into one line; must be separate numbered items.
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 2: lettered principles a–m are run together (e.g., 'include: a.' on same line; 'f.' and 'g.' merged; 'andm.' merged).
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 3: lettered items d–f are merged into one line.

Scrambled/incorrect numbering structure in Article 4: original has items (1), (2), (3) but translation shows 1., (2), 3. (missing (2) marker consistency and wrong marker for item 3).
Meaning drift in Article 4(1)(c): 'pertanyaan yang menjerat' is closer to 'leading/trapping questions' than 'ensnaring questions' (minor but legal nuance).

Scrambled/merged list structure: in multiple places the lettered items (a., b., etc.) are run together on the same line as the preceding text (e.g., Article 5(1), 5(2), Article 10, Article 11(1), Article 12, Article 13, Article 14), whereas the original has distinct a–g items in order. This can break downstream boundary-based retrieval.

Minor meaning drift/term choice: Article 14(c) translates "permohonan penetapan perlindungan" as "protection orders"; the original is an application for a determination/decision of protection (not necessarily a court order).

Scrambled/merged list structure: in Article 2, Point h and Point i are run together in one paragraph; Point l and Point m are run together in one paragraph. These should be separated to preserve item boundaries matching the original markers.
